Odin wins by preserving a defect.

On his first move Odin writes 3 in a box. Call a box defective if it contains a number greater than 1. Whenever Evelyn modifies the only defective box so that it is no longer defective, Odin uses a fresh empty box and writes 3 there. On every other move he writes 1 in a fresh empty box whenever possible.

Before Evelyn has produced k zeros, at most k of her moves have been spent writing zeros, and Odin has made at most one fresh-box move per such round. Since there are 3k boxes, a fresh empty box is available whenever Odin needs one to preserve a defective box. If Evelyn instead spends moves decreasing a defective box, the number of zeros is not increasing, giving Odin still more time.

Consequently, when the kth zero is produced, some other box still contains a number greater than 1. The special terminal condition therefore fails, and Odin wins. If the game ends because a player cannot move earlier, the other player wins; under the strategy, that player is Odin. Hence Odin has a winning strategy: \(\boxed{\text{Odin}}\).

Decreasing moves by Evelyn only reduce the number of zeros and cannot worsen this count.
